text:
Maya: Heads up — after the NF4/FP4 canary at 4% we saw a 22% drop in tokens/sec on prefill-heavy routes :eyes:
Sam: saw that too, p95 latency up ~180ms and memory on a few hosts spiked by ~3.1GB around the same time
Li: timeline? did we change kernel selector or scheduler flags during the canary?
Maya: no selector config change, but the canary included the new calibration profile (calib-v2) plus the fp4 kernel bundle
DeployBot: Canary nf4-fp4-calib-v2 rolled to hostgroup: infer-canary-4pct at 2026-03-15T09:12:43Z
Ben: I profiled a slow host — kernel selection started preferring the small-block fp4 kernel after a mid-batch thermal window. GPU clock polled and dropped to 1050MHz which seems to force a different kernel path
Cassie: thermal? weird. are we hitting thermal throttling or PCIe power caps?
Sam: looks like throttle. dmesg on the host shows repeated GV100 freq down events during bursts; coincides with long prefill windows where many small requests queue up
Li: that would change latency distribution and make batching heuristics choose more microbatches, increasing KV cache churn
Maya: exactly. KV hit ratio dropped from 87% -> 63% on affected hosts, which explains memory churn (more slab allocations) and extra memcpy spikes
Ben: attached quick perf snapshot (trimmed):
```
perf top -p 1234 -g --sort comm --no-children
  23.4%  kernel_fp4_small_block
  18.1%  cuda_memcpy_async
  12.7%  kv_cache_lookup
  9.2%   scheduler_enqueue
```
Cassie: that kv_cache_lookup number is alarming for nf4 workloads — should be mostly cached prefill keys
Sam: hypothesis: calibration changed tokenization pad distribution (calib-v2 pads longer for safety), that increases prefill seq length and shifts batch shape to longer prefill tails -> bigger KV working set -> more fragmentation under current slab allocator
Li: also note mixed-precision path chooses fp4 small-block kernels when clock < 1200MHz in our kernel selector heuristics. Thermal throttle toggles kernel choice mid-request, causing oscillation in throughput as we hit slowpath memcpy/packing code
Maya: action items I propose: 1) revert calib-v2 from canary, 2) flip selector to prefer stable nf4 kernel until cooling/telemetry fixed, 3) enable KV conservative prefill compaction for affected hosts
Ben: +1. I'll open a bisect to verify selector threshold sensitivity — want to quantify tokens/sec vs frequency boundary
Sam: I'll add a thermal telemetry flag to the host agent to dump GPU freq histograms and slab allocator fragmentation every 5s for the canary group
Cassie: I'll instrument the KV cache metrics to surface per-sequence prefill lengths and eviction rates in Console (route-level) so we can correlate to user workloads
Li: small rollback note: if we revert calib-v2, we'll also re-run a quick quality pass: some prompts regressed slightly in BLEU for low-temp runs — need to confirm it's not a calibration-only issue
Maya: agreed. schedule: revert calib-v2 now, hold kernel selector change behind canary toggle, gather telemetry for 12h, then revisit. If tokens/sec still low after revert, we'll rollback fp4 kernel bundle too
DeployBot: Rollback request submitted: rollback calib-v2 -> calib-v1 for hostgroup infer-canary-4pct at 2026-03-15T09:32:10Z by Maya
Ben: preliminary numbers after rollback start: tokens/sec up ~6% on one host, KV hit ratio creeping back to 75%
Sam: keep an eye on thermal histograms — if frequent throttles >30s then we need infra-level cooling or throttle-aware scheduler changes
Cassie: noted. I'll post an update to the console dashboard and leave annotations for the window 09:10-10:00 UTC
Maya: thanks all. If anyone gets a strong repro (single-run that shows oscillation) paste it here. For now I'm pausing the fp4 rollout until we have selector change plus telemetry
Li: filing an eng-runtime ticket with logs + perf traces: ER-4219
Maya: :thumbsup:
